questions.q: Which disaccharide is a non-reducing sugar?
questions.explain: In sucrose, C1 of glucose is bonded to C2 of fructose, so both anomeric carbons are used in the glycosidic bond and no free aldehyde group can form.
Lactose (milk sugar) is β-D-galactose linked C1 to C4 of D-glucose. Writing two glucose molecules is the common error.

options: The carbon atoms joined by the glycosidic bond
The configuration of the glycosidic bond, α(1→4) versus β(1→4)
questions.explain: Both are two D-glucose units joined C1 to C4 and both are reducing; maltose (from starch) has an α link and cellobiose (from cellulose) a β link.

questions.q: Sucrose (+66.5°) is hydrolysed to an equimolar mixture of D-glucose (+52.5°) and D-fructose (−92.4°). The approximate specific rotation of the mixture is
questions.explain: For a 1:1 mixture, (52.5 − 92.4)/2 ≈ −20°. The stronger laevorotation of fructose inverts the sign from (+) to (−), hence the name invert sugar.
